Return contract is now three-valued: `Infinity` (no markers), `null` (unmeasurable: non-finite clock, unparseable `marker.at`, or negative/future-dated age), otherwise a finite non-negative age. Every previously-`0` return path now returns `null`. Traced against both call sites, the blocking outcome is identical to the pre-change behavior in every case — `0 >= minimumMarkerAgeMs` was false and `null`-guarded `markerAgeMeasurable` is false, so no path that previously blocked can now clear. The change only refines the *reason* and *exit code*, never the *decision*. Confirmed there is no arithmetic on the possibly-`null` value at either site (`!== null` / `=== null` guards, then `>=` comparison only), so no coercion hazard exists.\n\n2. Exit-code discrimination. `gateExitCode()` correctly preserves the prior precedence (`keys?.length` → `EXIT.DUPLICATE` first), and only the single `VERIFICATION_REASON.INDEX_LAG` gate reason maps to 20. Poll exhaustion and search failure both return `SEARCH_UNAVAILABLE`, unmeasurable age returns `MARKER_AGE_UNMEASURABLE`, and `submit`'s separate retry-verification path never routes through `gateExitCode` — all three correctly remain exit 2, matching both the doc text and the dedicated regression test.\n\n3. Evidence quality. The round-11 gap is genuinely closed. The `npm test` output is file-granular, but Node's test runner only emits a file-level `✔` when every subtest in that file passes, so `✔ tests/jira-queue.test.mjs` is a valid entailment of the 57 in-file `test()` blocks passing — the packet's reconciliation of the \"9\" vs \"57\" counts is correct, not hand-waving. The `grep -n` inventory is exhaustive for the file and shows exactly one definition plus the two reviewed call sites.\n\n4. Test coverage matches the semantic split. The new tests exercise both sides of the discriminator (parseable-below-floor → 20, unparseable → 2, future-dated → 2), all three blocked commands, and the exit inventory assertion is tightened with explicit `EXIT.STATE_ERROR === 2` / `EXIT.INDEX_LAG_BLOCKED === 20` pins plus the retired-10–12 guard. Exit 20 is well within the safe 0–125 range and collides with nothing.\n\nNo changes requested.
